plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that produces goblet-shaped pink-lilac flowers in autumn, appearing without leaves. The leaves emerge the following spring and die back by early summer. Often called 'naked ladies' because the blooms appear leafless.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Native to Europe, including damp meadows in the UK, Germany, and France; widely cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxin that is also used medicinally to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Aster novi-belgii
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with masses of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It is a vital late-season nectar source for bees and butterflies, including migrating monarchs.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Native to eastern North America from Newfoundland to Georgia; naturalized in Europe and cultivated widely in gardens
plants.funFact: The common name 'Michaelmas daisy' comes from the feast of St. Michael on September 29, which falls right at the peak of its bloom in Britain.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, fast-growing tree that bursts into spectacular clouds of lavender-blue trumpet-shaped flowers just before its fern-like leaves emerge. Streets lined with jacarandas turn into purple tunnels, and fallen blossoms carpet the ground.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (September to November)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in Pretoria and Johannesburg in South Africa, Australia, and New Zealand's northern regions
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are around 70,000 jacaranda trees, giving it the nickname 'Jacaranda City,' and Australian university students traditionally believe that a flower falling on your head means you'll pass your exams.

plants.name: Tagetes erecta
plants.description: A tall, robust annual with large, pom-pom-like flower heads and pungent, finely divided foliage. It blooms prolifically until frost and is a staple in cottage and vegetable gardens for deterring pests.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through autumn (June to first frost)
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide in gardens and as a commercial crop for pigment
plants.funFact: In Mexico, these flowers are called cempasúchil and are used to decorate altars and guide spirits during Día de Muertos, celebrated at the start of November, so growers time their bloom for late September onward.
